newsitem.title: JAPAN: KPC offers term naphtha at $20 premium - traders.
newsitem.headline: KPC offers term naphtha at $20 premium - traders.

text.p: Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) has proposed raising the price of its term naphtha cargoes to $20 per tonne over the mean of Middle Eastern quotes for annual contracts starting in August, traders said on Wednesday.
This compares with term premiums of $7.90 for one-year supply contracts that started in August 1996, and $13.50 for term supplies during March 1997 to February 1998.
"KPC proposed a price of $20, while one of the buyers in the talks bid at $13.50," one trader said.
Rough levels of the new premium are expected to become clearer over the weekend or by early next week, after the first round of talks between KPC and each potential buyer is completed, traders said.
In the negotiations currently taking place in London, KPC is trying to justify a rise in term naphtha premiums citing a growing appetite for the petrochemical feedstock in Asia.

Whereas potential buyers, about a dozen firms from Japan and South Korea, have argued that spot markets in Asia have been relatively weak because of an inflow of arbitrage cargoes from the West and that KPC material is full-range naphtha, which is less popular as petrochemical feedstock than paraffinic naphtha, traders said.
Paraffinic naphtha yields more ethylene than full-range material, and is usually priced about $2.00 to $3.00 per tonne above full-range naphtha.
Japan and South Korea are expected to buy about a total of two million tonnes of Kuwaiti naphtha during the new term year starting August, traders said.
